breakdown.description: Inviscid flow assumptions are incompatible with the no-slip condition
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly identified that an inviscid fluid is incompatible with a no-slip condition. It resolved this by changing the fluid type to 'viscous', which is one of the valid corrections suggested by the ground truth. The generated specification begins with 'Model a viscous, incompressible, steady, two-dimensional laminar boundary layer flow...'

breakdown.description: No-slip condition requires viscosity to generate shear stress at the wall
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly understood that viscosity is required for a no-slip condition. The entire generated specification is built around a viscous flow problem (the Blasius problem), explicitly mentioning 'viscous' fluid, 'dynamic viscosity', and 'kinematic viscosity', thereby resolving the inconsistency in line with the ground truth.
